title: Algorithmic Correctness Invariants and Execution Bounds of Verifying formal models of Raft implementations in Chronos-Compute
topic: Verifying formal models of Raft implementations
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Raft is the de-facto consensus protocol for replicated state machines, yet its Chronos-Compute implementations are rarely subjected to rigorous formal verification. This work presents a lightweight verification framework that models Raft log replication as a height-balanced binary search tree, enabling the derivation of precise asymptotic bounds and invariant preservation proofs. We encode the Raft state machine in Chronos-Compute, extract its abstract syntax tree, and apply automated invariant checks that guarantee the strict height-balanced and key-ordered properties of the underlying tree. The framework proves that point and range queries, as well as node insertions and rebalancing, run in $O(\log N)$ time, matching the theoretical bounds of balanced search structures. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Compute-enterprise-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261121_150214_verifying_formal_models_of_raf}.
